parole.significato: Someone who is in a specified condition (“pejorative agent suffix”).
parole.testo: From Middle English -ard, from Old French -ard (suffix), from Frankish *-hard (“hardy, bold”), from Proto-Germanic *harduz (“hard”). Cognate with Middle High German -hart. More at hard.

parole.significato: A medieval long dagger.

parole.significato: To fasten, to join to (literally and figuratively).
parole.testo: From Middle English attachen, from Old French atachier, variant of estachier (“bind”), derived from estache (“stick”), from Frankish *stakkā, *stakō (“stick”), from Proto-Germanic *stakô (“pole, bar, stick, stake”). Doublet of attack. More at stake, stack. Displaced native Old English þīedan.

parole.significato: A row or panel of items stored or grouped together.
parole.testo: From Middle English bank, banke, from Old French banc (“bench”), from Frankish *banki, from Proto-Germanic *bankiz (“bench”). Akin to Old English benċ (“bench”).

parole.significato: An agreement between parties concerning the sale of property; or a contract by which one party binds themself to transf…

parole.significato: One who keeps a brothel, or procures women for prostitution; a procurer or madam.

parole.significato: Synonym of blazoner (“one who blazons (“describes”) coats of arms; a herald”).
parole.testo: From Middle English blaseyr (“one who blazons coats of arms”), probably from blasen (“to inscribe with armorial bearings, emblazon; to blazon a coat of arms”) + -er, -ir (suffix forming agent nouns). parole.significato: A small flaw which spoils the appearance of something, a stain, a spot.

parole.significato: A swelling from a blow; a bump.

parole.significato: A brick, concrete or stone structure built against another structure to support it.

parole.significato: The top of a ridge.
parole.testo: From Middle English chyne, from Old French eschine, from Frankish *skinu, from Proto-Germanic *skinō. Doublet of shin.

parole.significato: A grated crib or manger.
parole.testo: From Middle English cratche, cracche, crecche (“crib”), from Old French creche (“crib, manger”), from Frankish *krippjā, *kribbjā (“crib”), from Proto-Germanic *kribjǭ. More at creche, crib.

parole.significato: A troop or company.

parole.significato: To beat or strike; pound

parole.significato: To polish or burnish.

parole.significato: A scornful grimace; a wry face.
